newsitem.title: USA: Abbott says FDA clears Norvir for children.
newsitem.headline: Abbott says FDA clears Norvir for children.

text.p: Abbott Laboratories Inc said Friday it received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for the use of Norvir, a protease inhibitor, in children with HIV and AIDS.

Norvir is a first-generation protease inhibitor that has been shown to have a positive impact in the lives of AIDS patients, Abbott said. It said the drug was cleared by the FDA for marketing for adults on March 1, 1996.

Abbott said the use of Norvir was evaluated in 44 children who had completed at least four weeks of treatment as of September 30. The evaluation of the antiviral effect of Norvir in children is ongoing, the company said.
Abbott said the use of Norvir in children below age two has not been established as safe.
Side effects in HIV-infected children were similar to those seen in adults, including nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, loss of strength and taste disturbance.
